one_liner: Coordinates NOVA programs that let high school students earn college credit, working with Loudoun County high schools, students, families and college staff.
fit_summary: Daniel's coordination work at IEM (organizing FEMA onboarding data, helping stand up vaccination sites, a five-person intake team answering applicants' questions) and his ease with people transfer to a liaison-heavy coordinator role. Dual enrollment work usually calls for higher-education or K-12 advising experience, which his resume doesn't show, and the posting gives no details.
eligibility: The posting text is unavailable, so open the jobs.virginia.gov listing and confirm the minimum qualifications, any degree requirement, and whether this is a classified, wage, or faculty/administrative position.
Check whether a bachelor's degree or education/advising experience is required, which is common for NOVA coordinator roles.
Expect a background check for any role working with minors in high schools.
The job is based in Loudoun County with no remote option, so plan for commuting from Manassas to Loudoun campuses and high schools.
strategy: Read the full posting on jobs.virginia.gov first and copy its exact knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs) and duty phrases into your resume, since no description was provided here.

Frame your IEM work as stakeholder coordination for public-sector clients, such as liaising with agencies, organizing meetings or trainings, and tracking deliverables, using only duties you actually performed.
Emphasize your public-facing strengths, including explaining complex processes clearly, building relationships with partners like school counselors, and serving diverse community members.
Highlight any tutoring, mentoring, outreach, event planning, or education volunteer experience, because it directly supports dual enrollment work.
Virginia state applications allow longer resumes than federal ones, but fill in every application field completely and answer any supplemental questions with specific examples.
The closing date is not stated, so apply promptly because 'open until filled' postings can close without notice.
resume_bullets: Answered homeowners' questions at a five-person intake center for ReBuild NC after Hurricane Matthew (2019).
Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients, in person and virtually (2022–2024).
Worked with county governments to update their COVID-19 emergency grant applications (2020).
interview_questions: What do you know about dual enrollment, and why does it matter for Loudoun County students?
How would you build relationships with high school counselors and administrators who have competing priorities?
Tell us about a time you explained a complex process to someone unfamiliar with it.
How would you manage deadlines, registrations and records for many students across multiple schools?
watch_outs: Salary, grade and duties are not listed, so verify pay and role level before investing heavily in the application.
Education-sector experience may be required. A degree requirement is covered by his M.A. (George Mason, 2016); advising experience is the open question.
Possible travel between Loudoun high schools and campuses, plus seasonal peaks around registration periods.
